notes:
General: mid-market SaaS PM + Product org; core product is a helpdesk/engagement suite used by SMBs but growing into mid-market. Interested in pragmatic path: start Hosted API for fast rollout and then move critical customers to Dedicated for predictable latency/cost.

POC details: 2-week hosted POC using sample KB (~120k docs). Workloads: hybrid — chat for customer support (avg prompt+response tokens ~400), embeddings for semantic search/agent routing, reranking for top-k suggestions. Observed: p95 chat latency ~220ms with default settings during test harness; cost per chat request higher during rerank/beam phases.

Cost workshop highlights (02/23 workshop):
- Redwood Optimize ran a unit-economics model for their workload; baseline hosted unit cost estimated $0.045 per chat interaction at current tokenization/profile.
- Recommendations: enable request-level continuous batching for embeddings, implement prefix/KV caching for common KB prefixes, move reranking candidates to a lighter quantized model for first-pass, then heavy model fallback.
- Quantization experiments: int8 gave ~40-55% token-cost reduction; int4 promising but needs quality regression testing on edge cases.
- Batching guidance: increase request window for embeddings during peak to improve throughput; suggested 20-50ms batching window for their traffic shape to reduce tokens/second by ~30% while keeping median latency sub-200ms.
- Caching: TTL policy suggested 1h for recent KB queries, with LRU sized to typical session KV usage; expected hit rate 18-28% initially, improving with warmup.
- Expected impact: optimistic case 45% reduction in monthly inference spend; conservative case 20-25% after safety margins.

Security & Compliance: Cobalt Fern has enterprise customers that require SSO (SAML), SOC2 compliance, audit logs, and KMS integration for keys. Data residency: US primary, but 1 enterprise customer requires EU residency - uses VPC/dedicated. Legal flagged data retention and deletion SLAs; Redwood to provide security FAQ (drive link) and SOC2 reports.

Commercial: They want committed monthly throughput for high-value customers (Dedicated) + Hosted for long tail. AE discussed 12-month reserved pool with burst credits. Procurement wants a clear migration path and an exit/backout plan.

Quotes: VP Eng R. Matthews: "Costs kill feature adoption — if we can show a 30% win without hurting accuracy we can justify an enterprise plan."

Open tech questions / action items:
- Run a quality sweep on int8 vs fp16 on 200 edge queries (Marco / Redwood research) — target 2026-03-18.
- Produce Dedicated sizing spreadsheet + pricing addendum (deliver by 2026-03-15).
- SSO integration timeline: Cobalt Fern needs SAML metadata and test IdP; security team to review SEC-6031 ticket.
- Legal: review data residency clause for EU customer; provide sample DPA.
